support-triage-automation-state.title: Local support triage automation and progress
support-triage-automation-state.content:
An active RLM heartbeat performs hourly customer-inquiry triage. Heartbeat ID: 4c2ecee6-abcd-4c3d-8699-3103851288d1; label: hourly-support-triage; interval: 1h; delivery mode: follow_up.

Per-run workflow:
1. GET http://127.0.0.1:8128/batches/last and read integer last_seq.
2. GET http://127.0.0.1:8128/inquiries?after=<last_seq>; response is a list of up to 200 objects with integer seq and string text.
3. If empty, do not POST.
4. Otherwise classify every fetched inquiry exactly once through semantic understanding, not keyword matching: refund = wants money returned for a charge; bug = product behavior is broken or incorrect; sales = wants to buy, upgrade, obtain a quote, demo, pricing, or discuss expanded usage; other = anything else.
5. POST http://127.0.0.1:8128/batches with exactly three top-level keys: batch_start_seq (minimum fetched seq), batch_end_seq (maximum fetched seq), and classifications (one {"seq": int, "category": "refund|bug|sales|other"} per fetched inquiry, with no omissions or extras).

Progress: batches covering sequences 1–84 were successfully submitted. The latest requested manual run read last_seq 84 and fetched sequences 85–96, but no classification POST result has occurred yet. Resume by classifying that already-fetched set and submitting one batch for 85–96; avoid starting a second fetch unless runtime state has been lost, in which case re-read /batches/last before proceeding.

refinements.evidence: The workflow has been executed repeatedly and successfully through sequence 84, while the latest manual run fetched sequences 85–96 but has not yet classified or submitted them; persisting this state prevents duplicate fetching or lost progress.
refinements.outcome: Subsequent turns can resume the pending run by semantically classifying sequences 85–96 and posting exactly one batch, while retaining the heartbeat ID and validated API contract for future runs.
